HISTORY AND PHYSICAL (H&P)

History:
• 2-day history of gradually worsening, constant burning pain localized just below the umbilicus.  
• Associated symptoms: subjective fever/feeling hot and sweaty, mild nausea (no vomiting), increased urinary frequency, pink-tinged urine.  
• No dysuria, no flank pain, no diarrhea; constipation last week now resolved.  
• Bowels currently normal; passing urine without pain.  
• Last sexual intercourse 4 days ago with same partner; Implanon in situ ×1 year; last menstrual period ~2 weeks ago; pregnancy believed unlikely but not excluded.  
• No prior similar episodes.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic illnesses reported.  
• Surgical history: none.  
• Medications: Etonogestrel implant (Implanon) – dose/route/frequency not applicable; Trimethoprim prescribed today, one tablet twice daily for 3 days.  
• Allergies: not recorded.

Physical Examination:
• Teleconsultation – no in-person exam performed.  
• Vital signs: not recorded.  
• General appearance (as reported): patient able to ambulate, no shortness of breath, no chest pain, no headaches or visual changes.

Impression:
Probable uncomplicated acute cystitis (lower urinary tract infection) based on suprapubic pain, urinary frequency, and pink urine.  
DDx consistent with transcript:  
1. Acute cystitis – most likely given urinary symptoms and location of pain.  
2. Early appendicitis – consider if pain migrates or systemic symptoms worsen.  
3. Ectopic pregnancy – low likelihood but must be excluded in reproductive-age patient.

Management Plan:
• Empiric antibiotic: Trimethoprim 1 tablet PO twice daily for 3 days (as e-script to patient’s pharmacy).  
• Symptomatic relief: Paracetamol for pain (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Hydration advice; consider cranberry juice for urinary symptoms.  
• Obtain home urine pregnancy test today/tomorrow; report positive result immediately.  
• Safety-net instructions: seek review or ED care for worsening abdominal pain, vomiting, high fever, rigors, flank pain, syncope, or positive pregnancy test.  
• Follow-up: telephone or in-person review within a few days if no improvement or sooner if symptoms escalate.

Patient Summary:
Young woman with 2 days of suprapubic burning pain, urinary frequency, and pink urine, likely representing acute cystitis. Empiric trimethoprim started; pregnancy test advised; instructed to return if no improvement or deterioration.

Key Takeaways:
• Start trimethoprim today and complete full 3-day course.  
• Perform a pregnancy test as soon as possible; call clinic with result.  
• Return promptly for worsening pain, fever, vomiting, or other new symptoms.

Next Steps:
• Home urine pregnancy test.  
• Re-assessment in 2–3 days or sooner if condition worsens.  
• Consider urinalysis/urine culture and abdominal exam if symptoms persist or escalate.
